evidenceSource.primary: %TEMP%\covtrigb\ilspy\Modules — ilspycmd decompilation of the QA-profile interop assemblies (Modules-ASM, GameData-ASM, GlobalFramework-ASM)
evidenceSource.secondary: %TEMP%\enemytrig-ilspy — 7 hand-picked Enemies sources (AgentAI, EnemyBehaviour, EnemyDetection, EnemyLocomotion, ES_ScoutDetection, ES_ScoutScream); superseded by the full tree above
evidenceSource.method: ilspycmd decompilation of the interop wrapper; every signature below is the wrapper's own generated member, so a member that is not listed has no public interop wrapper and is not reachable from a BepInEx plugin
evidenceSource.notDoable: the IL2CPP interop wrappers carry no method bodies; a body's call sites (who calls ActivateState, what m_attackWindupDuration is read by) cannot be read from these sources, and the machine-readable dump used by sibling slices was not present in this session. Every claim below is therefore a *declaration-level* claim unless it says otherwise.

evidence.nativeEntry: Enemies.ES_EnemyAttackBase.ActivateState — two `public virtual` overloads, interop tokens 100683981 (Vector3, AgentAbility, int) and 100683982 (Agent, AgentAbility, int). Both dispatch through il2cpp_runtime_invoke on the object's own virtual method, so a call on a live ES_*Attack instance reaches the concrete override.
evidence.instanceSource: EnemyLocomotion exposes one field per attack state type: StrikerAttack (offsets registered under `StrikerAttack`), TankAttack, TankMultiTargetAttack, ShooterAttack, StrikerMelee — all `public` interop fields, so the state instance can be read from the enemy's own locomotion.
evidence.stateMachine: ES_Base is the shared base: `public virtual void Stop()` (token 100683857), `public virtual bool AllowedToForceState(ES_StateEnum)` (token 100683856), `public unsafe EnemyAI m_ai`, `m_enemyAgent`, `m_locomotion`, `m_stateEnum`. EnemyLocomotion exposes `CurrentStateEnum` (get), `ForceState(ES_Base)` (token 100683845), `ChangeState(ES_StateEnum)` (token 100683841), `AddState(ES_StateEnum, ES_Base)` (token 100683840).
evidence.attackFields: ES_EnemyAttackBase public fields: m_attackWindupDuration (float), m_lastAttackIndex (int, +0x54), m_attackDoneTimer (float, +0x58), m_performAttackTimer (float, +0x5C), m_attackTarget (Agent), m_lastSeenTargetPos / m_overrideAttackTargetPos / m_lastAimTargetPos (Vector3), m_lineOfSight (bool), m_attackWasPerformed (bool).
evidence.abilities: Enemies.EnemyAbilities public members: ActiveAbility (get), GetAbility(AgentAbility, int), IsAbilityReady(AgentAbility, int), UseAbility(AgentAbility) and UseAbility(AgentAbility, int), GetAbilities(ref List<AbilityEntry>, Il2CppStructArray<AbilityCondition>), HasAbility(AgentAbility).
evidence.target: AgentAI.m_target is a public interop field and AgentAI.SetTarget(Agent) / Target / IsTargetValid are public; EnemyAI overrides SetTarget(Agent).

blockers: The catalog row declares `ability` as `resource` with `resourceKind: ability` and `schema: forge.resource.ability`. No provider in the tree registers a resource kind named `ability`, so a plan naming this row cannot be loaded: the runtime refuses an unresolved resource reference at load (`stale-resource` / `resource-kind`), not at dispatch.

The catalog row has no `ability_index` input, and every native ability entry point that reaches a specific attack needs the index (`GetAbility(ability, index)`, `UseAbility(ability, index)`, `ActivateState(..., abilityIndex)`). `abilityIndex` is not derivable from anything else the row carries.

`ai_target` is an entity port. The native overload that takes a target needs an `Agent`; this provider can only resolve `Agent` instances of the kind it owns (`gtfo.enemy`), so a player or map-object reference cannot be turned into the native argument. The Vector3 overload would work around this but is not what the catalog's `ai_target` port means.

`phase_policy` declares `full` and `skip_windup`. Skipping the wind-up is a state-machine decision (`m_attackWindupDuration` is a field of the state instance, and the wind-up dispatch is the game's), so it cannot be expressed without writing the state's own fields — which is a direct field write, refused by the slice's native-write rule.
capabilities.hostClientVisibility: not-established. `AgentMode` and `EB_States` are the AI values `EnemySync.m_aiStatePacket` replicates (`pEnemyStateData`: target, agentMode, behaviourState); no shipped packet carries an `ES_StateEnum` or an `ES_*Attack` activation, so whether a host-side ActivateState call produces the same attack on a client is unproven. An action claimed to be host-authoritative must not rest on that.

evidence.stop: ES_Base declares `public virtual void Stop()` (interop token 100683857). A full-tree scan of the decompiled Enemies namespace finds **no override of Stop in any ES_* or EB_* type**: `Select-String -Pattern 'override void Stop\(\)'` over Modules\Enemies\*.cs returns zero matches, as does the same scan over Modules\*.cs. The row's own note (base slot 19 pointing at a shared thunk) is consistent with this: on this build the member has no real body behind it, so a call would be recorded as a commit while producing no observable effect.
evidence.stateGate: ES_Base.AllowedToForceState(ES_StateEnum) is virtual and overridden by ES_StrikerAttack (token 100684120) and ES_TankMultiTargetAttack (token 100684179), so a forced transition can be refused by the state that is running — but that is a gate on entering a state, not an interrupt of one.

blockers: The catalog row's recipient input is `behaviors`, `type: handle`, `handleKind: lease`, `lifetime: entity_life`. Handles are minted by a provider through the kernel's handle pool; nothing in the tree mints a behaviour lease, so a plan cannot name a value for this port. The slice's own instruction is explicit: a row that needs a handle to resume or interrupt later is reported as not implemented.
Even with a handle, the instance it named would have to be an instance this provider started; the game keeps no cancellable-behaviour registry, and `Stop()` has no effect on this build.

evidence.limbType: Dam_EnemyDamageLimb derives from UnityEngine.MonoBehaviour (not from Dam_SyncedDamageBase) and is a per-limb component reached through Dam_EnemyDamageBase.DamageLimbs.
evidence.writableFields: IL2CPP.GetIl2CppField registrations exist for all four surveyed fields: m_healthMax, m_health, m_weakspotDamageMulti, m_armorDamageMulti (Dam_EnemyDamageLimb.cs lines 1214-1217; each has a public getter and setter writing through IL2CPP.il2cpp_field_get_offset). They are readable and writable from a plugin.
evidence.publicApi: Dam_EnemyDamageLimb public API: m_limbID, m_base, m_type, m_ignoreGlue, IsDestroyed, m_health, m_healthMax, m_weakspotDamageMulti, m_armorDamageMulti, DoDamage(float), HealthRel(), HasDestruction(), DestroyLimb(sDestructionEventData), ApplyWeakspotAndArmorModifiers(float,float), ApplyDamageFromBehindBonus(...), TestDamageModifiers(float,float), SetBaseDamagable(Dam_EnemyDamageBase), GetHealthRel(), and the damage entry points (BulletDamage, ExplosionDamage, MeleeDamage, ...).
evidence.replication: The only replication in this area is packet-driven damage. Dam_SyncedDamageBase carries one SNet_Packet per damage channel — m_setHealthPacket (pSetHealthData), m_bulletDamagePacket (pBulletDamageData), m_explosionDamagePacket, m_meleeDamagePacket, m_addHealthPacket, and 15 more — plus `public void SendSetHealth(float)` (token 0x161F790 per the existing e10 evidence) for the base health. There is no packet, setter or receive path for m_health, m_healthMax, m_weakspotDamageMulti or m_armorDamageMulti: a host-side field write changes only the host's limb, and the row's own note already says so ('writing the host's local field makes host and client damage calculation diverge').

blockers: There is no synced limb-health entry point in this build. Writing the field is exactly the direct-field write the slice's hard rule refuses; the alternative (apply damage through the replicated damage entry points so every peer reaches the same limb state through the game's own pipeline) is a different capability — it is `forge.action.combat.damage` with a limb port, which this provider already implements.

`armor` and `weakspot` (m_armorDamageMulti / m_weakspotDamageMulti) are local damage multipliers with no replication at all; the catalog's own note asks for a ruling on whether host/client divergence is allowed, which this slice cannot make.

`break_policy` (detach / disable / none) has no native counterpart that is a *profile* write: DestroyLimb(sDestructionEventData) is reached through the replicated damage path, and calling it directly on the host would once more be a one-sided write.

evidence.instanceFields: EnemyDetection public instance fields, all writable through IL2CPP: m_movementDetectionDistance, m_detectionBuildupSpeed, m_detectionCooldownSpeed, maxAttackDistance, m_noiseDetectionOn, m_noiseDetectionRange, m_noiseDetectionValue, m_biggestDetectionBuildup, m_biggestDetectionTarget, plus static scratch state (s_delta, s_targetVisMod, s_targetNoiseMod, s_viewconeMul/Sub, s_behaviourData, ...).
evidence.setup: EnemyDetection.Setup(EnemyAI) is public (token 0x...822636 window) and is the member that populates those fields from the behaviour data; UpdateData() and UpdateTargets() are public frame members.
evidence.behaviourData: The behaviour data behind it is EnemyBehaviourData (a block type: EnemyBehaviourDataBlock), which the note below covers.
evidence.noReplication: No SNet_Packet, no setter and no receive path carries any perception value. The enemy replication structs are pEnemyStateData (target, agentMode, behaviourState), pExtraBehaviourStateData (bossPhase) and pEnemyPathData; none of them holds a range, a speed or a light-sensitivity value.

blockers: A host-side write to m_movementDetectionDistance / m_noiseDetectionRange / m_detectionBuildupSpeed changes only the host's detection. Detection decides when the host's AI attacks, so the host and its clients would disagree about the same enemy's awareness — the exact divergence the slice's native-write rule refuses.
The `profile` resource port has the same unresolved-provider problem as `attack`'s `ability` port: no provider registers `forge.resource.profile`, so a plan naming this row cannot load.

`light_response` (ignore / scaled / strict) has no native member in the decompiled wrapper: the view-cone and light modifiers are the static locals listed above, shared by every enemy on the peer, so they cannot express a per-recipient setting.

evidence.nativeMember: Enemies.SquidBossBehaviour.Phase — `public unsafe int Phase { get; set; }`, interop tokens 100683628 (get) / 100683629 (set), backed by `<Phase>k__BackingField` (field registration on line 1260). The property is an auto-property: there is no validation and no side effect in either accessor.
evidence.nativeWrite: The setter is called through the game's own object: `il2cpp_runtime_invoke(NativeMethodInfoPtr_set_Phase_Public_set_Void_Int32_0, IL2CPP.Il2CppObjectBaseToPtrNotNull((Il2CppObjectBase)this), ptr, ...)` writes the native field. A call from managed code therefore reaches the same field the game's own code writes.
evidence.nativeConsumer: SquidBossBehaviour.ActivateWeakspotIfNeeded() — `public unsafe void ActivateWeakspotIfNeeded()` (token 100683644). The decompiled wrapper lists no other member that reads `Phase`; the only reader the interop exposes is this step, so the handler calls it after the setter rather than leaving the phase unread.
evidence.replication: SquidBossBehaviour overrides `GetExtraStateDataForCapture()` (returns EnemySync.pExtraBehaviourStateData) and `SetIncomingExtraStateData(pExtraBehaviourStateData)`, the pair EnemyBehaviour declares virtual. The payload struct carries exactly one field — `public byte bossPhase` — and travels over `EnemySync.m_aiExtraBehaviourStatePacket` (SNet_Packet<pExtraBehaviourStateData>). This is the game's own per-frame capture of the boss phase, so a host-side write through the setter is captured and sent by the game itself; Forge does not need a replication path of its own.
evidence.domain: The replicated field is one byte, so the wire domain is 0..255. The setter itself does not bound the value, so the handler enforces the domain before the write instead of letting the wire truncate it.
evidence.restriction: Only SquidBossBehaviour carries the field. `ai.m_behaviour` is declared as EnemyBehaviour, so the handler proves the instance really is a boss before touching it: a plain EnemyBehaviour is refused with `not-a-phase-receiver`, never treated as phase zero.
evidence.unproven: Whether any *other* game logic reacts to a phase change is not readable from the interop wrappers (the generated code carries no bodies). The handler therefore claims only the value it wrote and read back, calls the one public consumer the interop exposes, and refuses `reset_policy: reset` rather than pretending a state-machine restart.

capabilities.hostClientVisibility: host-authoritative by construction: the value is written on the host, and the host's own capture pass (`GetExtraStateDataForCapture` → `m_aiExtraBehaviourStatePacket`) is what a client applies through `SetIncomingExtraStateData`. The `Phase` accessors report CallerCount(0) in the wrapper, i.e. they are reached through the replication/behaviour machinery rather than by name in IL; the capture pair and the byte-wide payload are the declaration-level proof that the value is replicated.
